title: eCPRI: add payload dissector preference
description: Make it possible to select the dissector for parsing the eCPRI payload

notes.body: This is not the right way to go about this.  You want to set up a dissector table for dissect_ecpri() to call and have protocols use Decode As.

I would like to ask - is this a proprietary variation of the standard protocol?  If so, is this the most appropriate place to configure differences?  I am aware of other variations of the standard protocol that could possibly be handled in a more granular way, e.g., for u-plane, the headers would be unchanged but the payload would differ..

Hi @mmann78 and @martin.r.mathieson 

Thanks both for commenting on this merge request and Happy new year!

What I wish to accomplish: I would like to be able to dissect "the O-RAN" part (i.e. the eCPRI payload) using a dissector plugin.

Currently the eCPRI dissector unconditionally calls the built-in O-RAN dissector on the payload, so I thought this was the least intrusive way of accomplishing what I wanted.

The alternative I see to accomplish this with the current state is to make a proprietary dissector plugin of the eCPRI dissector too, in which you can select what dissector to use for the eCPRI payload.  My thought was simply that other people in the community was facing the same challenge as I was.  However, I would love to understand if there was another way.

@mmann78 I agree that a dissector table would be nice, but I'm not sure that the eCPRI transport offers a nice parameter to index a dissector table.  If e.g. carried by UDP we can use port number, but on raw Ethernet it is harder.

@martin.r.mathieson At this point, this is the standard O-RAN protocol with some recent in-standardization work items added, together with optional decoding of userplane data.  When we are done with this I would be happy to make a merge request on the O-RAN dissector, too.

Why do I wish to be able to have an O-RAN dissector plugin ? This O-RAN CUS protocol is in active development under standardization and we are experimenting with a number of different O-RAN like protocols.  The developers of the wireshark dissectors are a different crowd from the users of wireshark at our company.  It is so much easier to keep track of dissector plugins than different forks of the whole wireshark source code.  Also, we can have our integration teams use a stable release of wireshark, while providing latest-and-greatest plugins for our protocols.

The line in packet-epri.c:
`
if (call_dissector_only(oran_fh_handle, fh_tvb, pinfo, tree, &msg_type))
`

Should be able to be replaced with a dissector table, with a "targeted" API.  There are several protocols that don't have a "key identifier" for their payload like Ethernet, IP and TCP/UDP.  In this case you can use register_decode_as_next_proto() (see packet-socketcan.c for example). Then the "payload dissectors" register with that dissector table using dissector_add_for_decode_as() (see packet-j1939.c corresponding to the CAN dissector table)

Thanks @mmann78 for the excellent pointers.  With your suggested changes, I now have a somewhat working setup.  However, I don't know to make "O-RAN FH CUS" the default (pre-selected) sub-dissector for eCPRI payload.  If starting from a fresh setup, I need to manually do e.g. Analyze -\> "Decode as" and select "O-RAN FH CUS", even though it's the only option.

In `proto_register_ecpri()` I added:

`subdissector_table = register_decode_as_next_proto(proto_ecpri, "ecpri.subdissector", "eCPRI payload dissector", NULL);`

And in `proto_reg_handoff_oran`:

```
dissector_add_for_decode_as("ecpri.subdissector", oran_handle);
```

Any suggestions ?
